page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The compute topology allocates 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core utilizing two execution threads. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance paired with throughput constraints typical of a dual-thread single physical core. Single-core evaluations recorded a stress-ng score of 1942.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1648.0. In multi-threaded testing, the instance reached a Geekbench score of 2047.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1991.97. Uncached memory throughput recorded 21.51 GB/sec for large block reads and 14.04 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations registered at 1604.83, while Redis achieved 2.56 million SET operations per second.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the E2s_v6 provides efficient memory capacity relative to compute footprint. Because compute allocation is tied to a single hyperthreaded core, high-concurrency CPU tasks face resource contention. All file system requirements must be met using network-attached storage due to the absence of local disks. This instance is best configured for small relational databases, memory-backed caching layers like Redis, staging environments, and light enterprise applications requiring high memory capacity with modest computational load.
